Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Apex Energy Corporation Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] Please note this event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Alex Rivera, VP of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Apex Energy Corporation's Q3 2024 earnings call. Joining me on the call today are Mike Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Jenkins, Chief Financial Officer; David Lee, Chief Operating Officer; Robert Chen, VP of Exploration; and Lisa Patel, VP of Marketing.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we make today may be forward-looking. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks.

I will now turn the call over to Mike Thompson.

Mike Thompson: Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. Apex Energy Corporation delivered solid results in Q3 2024, driven by strong operational performance and favorable commodity prices. We achieved outstanding environmental performance, including zero Tier 1 spills and significant reductions in reportable spill volumes. I'm particularly pleased with our realized prices for oil and gas, bolstered by effective hedging that captured meaningful uplifts. Our refining segment showed resilience with high throughput and superior margins. The midstream business hit record transportation volumes amid key infrastructure expansions. We continued to drive down operating expenses per BOE through innovative cost controls. Finally, production volumes grew meaningfully both quarter-over-quarter and year-over-year across our portfolio.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Sarah Jenkins to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Sarah Jenkins: Thank you, Mike. As Mike highlighted, we had a strong quarter. Our revenue was $5.6 billion, up 18% year-over-year. Operating income was $1.25 billion, and net income was $875 million. We generated $1.3 billion in free cash flow and returned $550 million to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases. Our balance sheet remains strong, with $15.2 billion in debt and $3.1 billion in cash.

Before moving to operations, let me expand on a few key areas starting with our environmental performance, spills, incidents, and remediation efforts. Environmental stewardship is core to our license to operate, cost structure, and long-term value creation amid demands for lower-carbon oil and gas. We're proud of another strong quarter with zero Tier 1 spills—our most serious category under API Recommended Practice 75, defined as exceeding 1,000 barrels or causing significant harm—and a 28% year-over-year drop in total reportable spill volume to 1.2 barrels equivalent across global operations.

For transparency, in Q3 we had 14 reportable spills under EPA and PHMSA guidelines, all Tier 3 or lower—minor surface sheens or pinhole leaks from third-party interfaces, netting under 0.5 barrels after recovery. This beats the Permian Basin industry average of 22 incidents per operator per IOGP data, with our spill rate at 0.02 barrels per million produced, improved from 0.03 last year. Our Lost Time Incident Rate for environmental events stayed at 0.12 per 200,000 man-hours, under the OSHA upstream benchmark.

In our U.S. onshore Permian assets, proactive integrity management on the 4,200-mile gathering system avoided any pipeline releases, using fiber-optic distributed acoustic sensing from OptaSense to catch 17 micro-anomalies early and prevent potential 50-barrel incidents. Gulf of Mexico deepwater platforms like Apex Sentinel FPSO had zero hydrocarbon releases during hurricane season, due to subsea BOP verification surpassing BOEM standards. Internationally, our North Sea JV with Equinor reported one 0.1-barrel synthetic-based mud release from a drilling riser, contained via ROV-deployed booms—far below OSPAR's 1-tonne limit.

Remediation closed 100% of Q2 incidents and 95% of prior open cases, with $4.2 million invested this quarter—flat year-over-year despite 15% production growth to 850,000 boe/d. Efficiency came from in-house bioremediation using Chevron-derived microbial consortia degrading 85% of BTEX in 14 days, cutting disposal costs 40% versus landfarming. A Delaware Basin 0.3-barrel crude release in July was bioremediated on-site for $15,000, restoring soil TPH below 100 ppm per Texas Railroad Commission, versus $75,000 for off-site thermal.

Strategically, we're advancing ahead of regs like EU CBAM and Biden's Methane Emissions Reduction Program with AI leak detection on 65% of Permian laterals via Palantir Foundry and FLIR drone thermography—dropping fugitive emissions 35% with 98% alert accuracy. Over 12,000 field personnel finished SpillWise digital training, cutting response times under 15 minutes. We aim for net-zero Scope 1&2 spills by 2028 via SLB's Actively Managed Completions and SpillX autonomous vessels offshore.

Financially, remediation underspend of $2.8 million boosted free cash flow by 3 cents per share. At $82/bbl WTI and $14/MMBtu LNG spots, this de-risks capex for CCUS like our $500 million Permian hub capturing 2 Mtpa CO2 by 2026. Full ESG report with GRI assurance comes next week.

Next, our realized pricing and hedging. Our diversified portfolio in Permian, Eagle Ford, and Appalachia gas captured premiums, with hedging buffering NYMEX swings. Q3 realized oil averaged $74.25 per barrel, up 8% from Q2's $68.80 and flat YoY, topping WTI's $73.45 with a $1.20 Permian differential—best in three quarters post Matterhorn pipeline expansions. Eagle Ford added $2.10 premium from LLS demand at Motiva and Phillips 66 refineries at 95%+ utilization.

Gas realized $2.62 per MCF, up 15% sequentially from $2.28 but down 12% YoY, beating Henry Hub $2.45 by 17 cents via Marcellus/Utica basis swaps for $0.25/MCF in Appalachia at TETCO M-3 $2.70. Blended $32.40 per BOE supported $425 million EBITDA.

Hedging covered 62% of Q3 production. Oil: 55% at $75/bbl swap floor, collars $70-$85, adding $1.85/bbl—vital amid OPEC+ hikes and 430 million barrel inventories. Unhedged would've been $72.40. YTD, $3.20/bbl gains or $85 million cash. Gas: 72% at $2.75/MMBtu swaps (~$2.60/MCF), collars $2.40-$3.50, $0.18/MCF uplift despite 18% Henry Hub drop. Appalachia basis swaps +$0.20 shielded Dominion South gaps.

Quick table: Oil Q3 realized $74.25 vs WTI $73.45, 55% hedged, +$1.85 uplift, Q4 48% at $72 floor, 2025 42% $70. Gas $2.62 vs $2.45, 72% hedged, +$0.18, Q4 65% $2.60 swap, 2025 58% $2.50.

Ahead, Q4 oil collars 48% $72-$82 for $70+ WTI upside from Red Sea. 2025 gas 58% at $2.90 winter forwards for Haynesville. Initiatives: algorithmic collars cut VAR 30%, 12 counterparties like JPMorgan/Goldman/BP with low collateral, weather-linked CME derivatives for Appalachia.

This yields 12% cash flow at strips, funding $400 million buybacks and $1.2 billion Permian development.

Turning to refining segment performance—throughput, margins, efficiency. It added $1.2 billion to EBITDA, up 15% YoY/8% QoQ from our 2.1 million bpd across eight refineries in Gulf Coast, Midwest PADD 2, Singapore JV.

Throughput 1.95 million bpd at 93% utilization—five-year Q3 high vs 88% last year—on distillate/gasoline demand at 9.2 million bpd EIA. Gulf Coast Port Arthur/Beaumont 1.1 million bpd 96%, heavy WCS/Maya slates maxing cokers/hydrocrackers. Midwest Joliet/Lima 450k bpd 91%, Bakken sweets via Enbridge. Singapore 350k bpd 94% on IMO 2020 distillates. Q4 guide 1.9-2.0 million bpd 92-95%, jet fuel +15% YoY.

Margins $28.50/bbl, $3 over 3-2-1 $25.40—48% distillates $32 ULSD, 28% gasoline $22, 12% jet $38. Gulf 2-1-1 $26.80 beat peers 10-15% via octane blending to 52% yields. Feed $72/bbl 5% under WTI, 60% Q4 cracks hedged $24 floors. YoY +22% from contango, natgas $2.50/MMBtu -18%. West Coast Martinez ULSD $18 vs $32 Gulf, idled 20% for renewables. Singapore $12.50 GRM vs $9 avg.

Efficiency: costs $5.80/bbl -12% YoY, EBITDA $12.50/bbl +16%. Light yields 82% via $150 million Port Arthur digital twin adding 1,500 bpd ULSD. Energy 85k BTU/bbl -8%, OGCI-aligned; Joliet 10 MW solar -$4 million steam. Maint capex $220 million: Beaumont alkylation piping, coker quench for Mayas to 4,500-day runs. Port Arthur TA 10% under $120 million, 24 vs 28 days. Variable $4.20/bbl, lubes +14% $45 million.

Gulf 65% EBITDA $18/bbl margins, exports 420k bpd. Midwest $22/bbl rail Bakken. West $14/bbl, Martinez $500 million renewables co-process 5k bpd waste oils for $2/bbl LCFS. Renewables diesel 12k bpd $55 D4 RINs. Hedged 70% 2025 $22 cracks, $1.2 billion capex for Singapore VLSFO hydrotreater, India 95-octane.

Refining de-risks upstream, targets $4.5-5.0 billion FY EBITDA.

Now midstream—transportation volumes, infrastructure. EBITDA $425 million +22% YoY/8% QoQ, 92% utilization vs 85% target.

Volumes record 2.85 MMBoe/d +18% YoY/5% QoQ. Crude 1.65 MMbbl/d +25% YoY, Permian 6.2+ MMbbl/d, Longhorn 750k bbl/d 98%, $0.75 Midland basis. EPIC 520k bbl/d. NGLs 850k bbl/d +12%, Mont Belvieu butane $0.85/gal, Nederland 1.2 million bbl cargoes. Gas 3.2 Bcf/d +7% QoQ, Waha 1.1 Bcf/d -$0.15 basis post Plaquemines LNG.

Permian 65% volumes, takeaway >14 MMbbl/d. Bakken Dakota 450k bbl/d. Gulf LNG exports 14 Bcf/d.

Infrastructure: $1.8 billion 2024 capex, 60% FID. Permian Highway 200-mile +300 MMcf/d to Cheniere Stage 3, $450 million 15-year take-or-pay EQT/Chesapeake 95%, early under budget 8%, first gas March $0.25/MMBtu. Gray Oak Eagle Ford 42-inch +400k bbl/d 75% complete Q3 in-service. ILI 1,200 miles EMAT remediated 98% anomalies -35% leak risk PHMSA. AI leak detect 40% lines RSI sub-1% false positives DOT methane. 25 stations electric -120k tCO2e.

85% fee-based 10-year contracts. $300 million Targa NGL stub 150k bbl/d 15% IRR. Tailwinds OPEC+, Permian rigs 300 Baker Hughes, LNG 16 Bcf/d 2026. Capex $1.8B 70% growth, 10-12% 2025 volumes, ROIC >12% vs 8% hurdle. Hedged 60% 2025 EBITDA.

Midstream compounds value future-proofed.

Finally, operating expenses per BOE trends and strategies. Q3 OpEx $9.82/BOE -6% QoQ from $10.45, -12% YoY from $11.18—11th straight quarter decline, lower Permian quartile vs $11-13 Enverus avg. Pacing under FY $9.90-10.30 guide.

Trajectory: 2021 $13.25 post-COVID inflation; 2022 $12.10 -9%; 2023 $10.35 -14%; Q3 2024 $9.82 -12%. Structural: LOE $5.40/BOE 55% -22% since 2021; G&T $2.85; processing $1.22; G&A $0.35. Permian $8.75/BOE 85% prod vs Eagle Ford $12.50, GoM $18.20. Delaware sub-$8 LOE 12,500-ft laterals.

Strategies: Halliburton DecisionSpace AI 70% pads predict failures -28% downtime, LOE $0.62/BOE $120 million saved. Water recycle 85% Delaware WaterBridge electrocoagulant -40% trucking $0.75/BOE; ESPs 60% $1.80/BOE 1,200-day runlife. Sand/chem 80% locked 2023 prices -18% landed; SLB Neuristics fracs 20/BOE savings. Divested $200M Bakken $15+/BOE; GoM tie-backs -10%; Seekir drones -$15M fines.

Guide FY $9.70-10.10, H2 better; sub-$9 by 2026 20% FCF $60 WTI. Moat for M&A like $1.2B Delaware.

I will now turn the call over to David Lee for an operational update.

David Lee: Thank you, Sarah. On the operational front, we continue to execute effectively, aligning with the production details Sarah outlined. Production averaged 850,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day overall, with oil at 74% cut reflecting optimized completions. To add color, Q3 total 850,000 BOE/d built on Q2 momentum +6% QoQ equivalent adjusted, +10% YoY scaled. Oil 629,000 bbl/d equiv +8% QoQ/12% YoY; gas/NGLs 221,000 BOE/d flat QoQ/+3% YoY prioritized. Permian 62% at 527,000 BOE/d +9%/15%; Eagle Ford 72,000 +2% YoY; GoM 29,000 +4% QoQ. Q4 guide 860-870k BOE/d. We successfully brought Permian Delaware pads online, expected to drive growth.

Now I will turn it over to Robert Chen for an update on our exploration activities.

Robert Chen: Thank you, David. We are excited about the potential of our exploration program. We recently completed a successful seismic survey in the Permian Basin and are planning to drill 12 exploration wells in the next year. We believe these wells have the potential to add significant reserves to our portfolio, de-risking future development.

Finally, I'll turn it over to Lisa Patel to discuss our marketing strategy.

Lisa Patel: Thank you, Robert. We are focused on optimizing our marketing strategy to maximize the value of our production. We are seeing strong demand for renewable diesel in the Gulf Coast market, and we are working to expand our customer base and strengthen relationships with existing customers. The impact of this product on our margins and sustainability goals is significant, with LCFS credits and RINs enhancing realizations.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from Joe Harris with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Joe Harris: Good morning. Can you provide more detail on production volumes total, oil, gas—QoQ and YoY changes?

Mike Thompson: Good morning, Joe. As Sarah and David covered, our Q3 volumes hit 850,000 BOE/d with strong growth profiles across regions, driven by Permian ramps and frac optimizations boosting oil cut to 74%. We're guiding modest sequential upside into Q4 while maintaining capital discipline.

Operator: Our next question comes from Mary Chen with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Mary Chen: Good morning. What are your expectations for realized prices and the impact of hedging programs?

Sarah Jenkins: Good morning, Mary. Our hedging layers provide solid floors—48% oil Q4 at $72, 65% gas—positioning us well for volatility, with YTD uplifts already adding substantial cash flow as detailed earlier.

Operator: Our next question comes from Tom Baker with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Tom Baker: Could you please provide more color on operating expenses per BOE trends and cost strategies?

David Lee: Thanks, Tom. Our sub-$10/BOE run-rate reflects AI maintenance, water recycling at 85%, and supply chain locks—structural declines enabling high FCF yields even at lower strips.

Operator: Our next question comes from Sue Lee with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Sue Lee: How will the results of the exploration program affect the company's future strategy?

Robert Chen: Great question, Sue. Positive seismic in Permian sets up reserve adds that extend our inventory 10+ years, prioritizing high-return drilling to support 5-7% annual growth without chasing marginal acres.

Operator: Our next question comes from Raj Patel with Citi. Please go ahead.

Raj Patel: What is the outlook for the new product in the coming years?

Lisa Patel: Morning, Raj. Renewable diesel outlook is bright with production scaling to 50,000 bpd by 2027, capturing $50+/bbl premiums via RINs/LCFS amid EPA mandates—key to our low-carbon transition and margin expansion.

Operator: There are no further questions at this time. I would like to turn the conference back over to Mike Thompson for closing remarks.

Mike Thompson: Thank you, Operator. In summary, we are pleased with our performance in Q3 2024. We remain focused on executing our strategy and delivering value to our shareholders. Thank you for joining us today.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
